Lemma
[differential of a diffeomorphism is an isomorphism]

↗ def:dc-ch0-2-9 ↗ def:dc-ch0-2-8

1. ch0:2.9If $\varphi :M_1\to M_2$ is a diffeomorphism then for every $p\in M_1$ the differential $d\varphi _p:T_pM_1\to T_{\varphi (p)}M_2$ is a linear isomorphism.
Proof

\sketch

Let $\psi =\varphi ^{-1}$. By the chain rule (section 1) applied to $\psi \circ \varphi =\mathrm{id}_{M_1}$ and $\varphi \circ \psi =\mathrm{id}_{M_2}$, $d\psi _{\varphi (p)}\circ d\varphi _p=\mathrm{id}_{T_pM_1}$ and $d\varphi _p\circ d\psi _{\varphi (p)}=\mathrm{id}_{T_{\varphi (p)}M_2}$. Hence $d\varphi _p$ is a two-sided invertible linear map, i.e. a linear isomorphism, with inverse $d\psi _{\varphi (p)}$.

□
